correctness.rationale: For every \(k\ge1\) and \(\ell\ge k+1\), the first \(k\) complete columns force the next column one rail at a time, giving \(Z\le2k\). An explicit integer matrix \(X\) with \(2(\ell-k)\) rows and \(2\ell\) columns has exact Gram support on the \(k\)-th ladder power. Same-rail endpoint and interior dot products agree with every required edge/nonedge; for cross-rail pairs the two zero extremal products occur only at the forbidden column gap \(k\). At smaller gaps each possible negative term (\(-4\) within the second rail or \(-2\) across a particular rail orientation) occurs at most once and cannot cancel its positive counterparts (\(7,58\) and \(10,24\), respectively). The boundary case \(k=1\) has no interior offsets and is covered directly. A block-triangular minor has repeated diagonal blocks \(\left(\begin{smallmatrix}1&1\\0&-1\end{smallmatrix}\right)\) of determinant \(-1\), so \(A=X^{\mathsf T}X\) is positive semidefinite of rank \(2(\ell-k)\) and nullity \(2k\). The universal inequalities \(M_+\le Z_+\le Z\) and \(M\le Z\) prove the four equalities. The standalone verifier constructs graph powers independently by BFS, checks all Gram nonzeros, full-rank minors and forcing sequences in 130 profiles, and brute-forces smaller forcing seeds in 12 profiles; the infinite conclusion comes from the proof, not those samples.

originality.rationale: Abiad–Flagg–Ghasemi Nezhad–Zeijlemaker (arXiv:2610.03892v1, §3, Proposition 11 and Conjecture 12) explicitly give only an upper bound and a conjecture for grid powers. They report a finite experimental range, not an all-length, all-power result for the two-row grid and not an exact positive semidefinite minimum-rank formula. The present explicit 2-dimensional sliding-window Gram representation proves the full two-row special case and its PSD strengthening. Tree powers, ordinary path powers, circulants and torus products do not imply the finite Cartesian ladder-power statement. Searches under the exact formula, equivalent graph descriptions, rank variants, and related database results found no covering published theorem, subject to residual indexing limitations.
residual_risks: An unindexed or incompletely described article might independently establish the same two-row grid-power formula.

value.rationale: This result resolves the all-length, all-exponent two-row case of an explicit recent grid-power zero-forcing conjecture and strengthens it to equal ordinary and PSD zero forcing and minimum ranks. The two-row strip is the first genuinely cyclic/nonpath Cartesian grid, and the explicit low-rank sliding-window Gram realization addresses the essential missing universal lower bound rather than restating the already-known forcing upper bound or a small experimental table. The result is a natural infinite-family theorem with reusable linear algebraic structure; no claim is made to resolve the full higher-width conjecture.
